# DRAFT FOR REVIEW BY A QUALIFIED FINANCE/ACCOUNTING OR REGULATORY-REPORTING PROFESSIONAL — NOT FINANCIAL, TAX OR INVESTMENT ADVICE

## 1. Answer (ask 2)

Minimum capital ratios a Board-regulated institution must maintain under 12 CFR 217.10(a)(1), **before any capital buffer or other add-on**:

| # | Ratio | Minimum | Cite | Verbatim regulatory text (as reproduced) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Common equity tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio | **4.5%** | 12 CFR 217.10(a)(1)(i) | "A common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5 percent." |
| 2 | Tier 1 capital ratio | **6.0%** | 12 CFR 217.10(a)(1)(ii) | "A tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent." |
| 3 | Total capital ratio | **8.0%** | 12 CFR 217.10(a)(1)(iii) | "A total capital ratio of 8 percent." |
| 4 | Leverage ratio | **4.0%** | 12 CFR 217.10(a)(1)(iv) | "A leverage ratio of 4 percent." |
| (5) | Supplementary leverage ratio (SLR) — **conditional, not a general minimum** | **3.0%** | 12 CFR 217.10(a)(1)(v) | "For advanced approaches Board-regulated institutions or, for Category III Board-regulated institutions, a supplementary leverage ratio of 3 percent." |

Lead-in text quoted verbatim: "A Board-regulated institution must maintain the following minimum capital ratios:" — 12 CFR 217.10(a)(1).

**Scope note on row (5):** the 3.0% SLR is not a requirement for every Board-regulated institution; it applies only to advanced approaches institutions or Category III institutions. The four-ratio answer to the question as asked is rows 1–4.

## 2. Basis, period and currency

- **Period / version:** the text of Part 217 as reproduced on the cited pages, fetched 2026-11-23T04:04:13Z–04:04:15Z; corroborated against the govinfo annual editions **CFR-2025 title 12 vol. 2** and **CFR-2026 title 12 vol. 2**. All five fetches state identical thresholds in §217.10(a)(1).
- **Currency:** not applicable — these are dimensionless regulatory capital ratios expressed in percent of a regulatory denominator, not monetary amounts. No dollar figures are stated in this memo.
- **Basis of each ratio (denominators), as reproduced:**
  - CET1 ratio = CET1 capital ÷ **standardized total risk-weighted assets** (217.10(b)(1)); for an advanced approaches institution that has completed the parallel run and received Board notification under 217.121(d), the CET1 ratio is the **lower of** the standardized and advanced-approaches calculations (217.10(d)(1)).
  - Tier 1 ratio = tier 1 capital ÷ standardized total risk-weighted assets (217.10(b)(2)); advanced approaches: lower of standardized and advanced (217.10(d)(2)).
  - Total capital ratio = total capital ÷ standardized total risk-weighted assets (217.10(b)(3)); advanced approaches: lower of standardized and advanced-approaches-adjusted total capital (217.10(d)(3)).
  - **Leverage ratio denominator is NOT in the reproduced excerpt.** The reproduced text stops at 217.10(b)(2) on the part-level page; paragraphs (b)(4)/(c)(4) defining the leverage ratio denominator were not captured. See Section 7.
- **Accounting basis:** regulatory capital, computed under Part 217 Subparts B–D (numerator definitions in 217.20–217.22; risk-weighted assets under the standardized and advanced approaches). Not GAAP equity.

## 3. Why these figures are the pre-buffer minimums (ask 1)

The reproduced text of 217.11 independently confirms that the 217.10(a) ratios are the base to which buffers are added, because the buffer is defined as the excess over them:

> "A Board-regulated institution that is subject to 12 CFR 225.8 or 238.170 has a standardized approach capital conservation buffer that is equal to the lowest of the following ratios, calculated as of the last day of the previous calendar quarter: (A) The ratio calculated by the Board-regulated institution under 217.10(b)(1) or (c)(1)(i), as applicable, **minus the Board-regulated institution's minimum common equity tier 1 capital ratio requirement under 217.10(a)**; (B) The ratio calculated ... under 217.10(b)(2) or (c)(2)(i) ... **minus the ... minimum tier 1 capital ratio requirement under 217.10(a)**; and (C) The ratio calculated ... under 217.10(b)(3) or (c)(3)(i) ... **minus the ... minimum total capital ratio requirement under 217.10(a)**." — 217.11(c)(2)(i), govinfo CFR-2026 edition (sha256 ce190823bded)

> "Notwithstanding paragraph (c)(2)(ii) of this section, if any of the ratios calculated by the Board-regulated institution under 217.10(b)(1), (2), or (3) ... is less than or equal to the Board-regulated institution's minimum common equity tier 1 capital ratio, tier 1 capital ratio, or total capital ratio requirement under 217.10(a), respectively, the Board-regulated institution's capital conservation buffer is zero." — 217.11

**Illustrative arithmetic (one input assumed, one sourced — labelled):**

| Line | Item | Value | Label |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Institution's CET1 ratio per 217.10(b)(1) | 7.0% | **ASSUMPTION — illustrative only, not a fact about any institution** |
| B | Minimum CET1 ratio per 217.10(a)(1)(i) | 4.5% | **SOURCED** (quote in Section 1) |
| C | Standardized approach capital conservation buffer = A − B | 7.0% − 4.5% = **2.5%** | Arithmetic per 217.11(c)(2)(i)(A) formula |

This demonstrates mechanically that the 4.5%/6.0%/8.0% figures are floors subtracted before any buffer is measured; a ratio at or below the floor produces a buffer of zero under 217.11. Nothing in this illustration is a statement of any institution's actual capital position.

## 4. Source inventory (ask 3)

| Ref | URL | Fetched (UTC) | sha256 (as reported) | What it establishes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/part-217/section-217.10 | 2026-11-23T04:04:14Z | 11713cd13188 | Full §217.10 incl. (a)(1)(i)–(v), (b)(1), (d)(1)–(3), (e) |
| S2 | http://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/chapter-II/subchapter-A/part-217/subpart-B/section-217.10 | 2026-11-23T04:04:14Z | 11713cd13188 | Same section, same hash — independent path, identical text |
| S3 | https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2026-title12-vol2/xml/CFR-2026-title12-vol2-part217.xml | 2026-11-23T04:04:14Z | ce190823bded | 2026 annual edition of Part 217; same (a)(1) thresholds; §217.11 buffer formula |
| S4 | https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title12-vol2/xml/CFR-2025-title12-vol2-sec217-10.xml | 2026-11-23T04:04:13Z | c804b50067be | 2025 annual edition of §217.10; same thresholds |
| S5 | https://ecfr.gov/current/title-12/part-217 | 2026-11-23T04:04:15Z | 419cb44bcd48 | Part-level page; same thresholds; different §217.11 cross-reference vintage (see Section 6) |
| S6 | http://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-12/chapter-II/subchapter-A/part-217/subpart-D/subject-group-ECFRd4c5e16bc7f97a2 | (listed as source) | — | Subpart D grouping; no additional ratio threshold identified |

**Source-note line reproduced for §217.10:** "78 FR 62157, 62285, Oct. 11, 2013, as amended at 78 FR 62286, Oct. 11, 2013" and "79 FR 57744, Sept. 26, 2014". These are the only amendment citations captured for §217.10; the tail of the source note was not captured, so the full "as amended" chain is not verified (see Section 7).

## 5. What the four ratios do NOT include (explicit exclusions per ask 1)

Excluded from the 4.5% / 6.0% / 8.0% / 4.0% figures, because they are separate requirements in 217.11 and related provisions:

- standardized approach **capital conservation buffer** (217.11(c)(2));
- **countercyclical capital buffer amount** (217.11, and the public-disclosure requirement referencing it);
- **GSIB surcharge** (217.11 and subpart H; "A global systemically important BHC must use its GSIB surcharge calculated in accordance with subpart H of this part ...");
- **leverage buffer** for a global systemically important BHC: "A global systemically important BHC has a leverage buffer that is equal to the global systemically important BHC's supplementary leverage ratio minus 3 percent, calculated as of the last day of the previous calendar quarter" (217.11) — note the 3% here is the SLR minimum from 217.10(a)(1)(v), and the buffer is the excess over it;
- any **PRA/supervisory add-on** under 217.10(e)(1): "Notwithstanding the minimum requirements in this part, a Board-regulated institution must maintain capital commensurate with the level and nature of all risks to which the Board-regulated institution is exposed."

## 6. Version-control observations for the reviewer

1. **Thresholds are stable across every fetch.** S1, S2, S3, S4 and S5 all reproduce "4.5 percent / 6 percent / 8 percent / 4 percent" (and the 3 percent SLR) identically. The answer is therefore not sensitive to which of these vintages is the "cited page".
2. **Cross-reference drift in 217.11, not in 217.10.** S5 (part-level) reproduces the buffer formula referencing "217.10(d)(1)(i)", "217.10(d)(2)(ii)", "217.10(d)(3)(ii)"; S3 (2026 annual edition) references "217.10(b)(1) or (c)(1)(i)", "(b)(2) or (c)(2)(i)", "(b)(3) or (c)(3)(i)"; S1/S2 reference "(b)(1) or (c)(1)(i)". This is version drift in §217.11's drafting, not a change in the §217.10(a) minimums, and does not alter the answer.
3. **Pending/effective amendment flagged in the 2026 edition:** "At 90 FR 55289, Dec. 1, 2025, §217.11 was amended, effective Apr. 1, 2026." This touches §217.11 (buffers), which the question excludes. No corresponding effective-date note was captured for §217.10.
4. **Community bank leverage ratio framework option (217.10(a)(2)):** "A qualifying community banking organization (as defined in 217.12), that is subject to the community bank leverage ratio framework (as defined 217.12), is considered to have met the minimum capital requirements in this paragraph (a) of this section." Such an institution's operative minimum is the CBLR in §217.12, not the four ratios above. The reproduced excerpts do not contain the numeric CBLR threshold, so it is not stated here.
5. **Insurance holding companies (217.11(e)):** insurance bank holding companies and insurance savings and loan holding companies subject to subpart J calculate their capital conservation buffer under 217.604; an insurance mid-tier holding company is not subject to 217.11. This affects buffers only, not the 217.10(a) minimums.
6. **Advanced approaches institutions:** the binding ratio is the **lower** of the standardized and advanced-approaches calculations (217.10(d)(1)–(3)); the 4.5/6/8 minimums themselves are unchanged, but the denominator that applies can be the advanced-approaches total risk-weighted assets.

## 7. Deliberately NOT stated (no source in the reproduced text) — do not treat as omissions by accident

| Item | Why not stated |
|---|---|
| Leverage ratio denominator (average total consolidated assets) and any supplementary leverage exposure definition | Paragraphs 217.10(b)(4)/(c)(4) were not present in the captured excerpts. Confirm against the full section before relying on the denominator. |
| Numeric maximum of the capital conservation buffer (commonly expressed as a percent of RWA) | Not numerically reproduced in the captured 217.11 text; only the formula (actual ratio minus 217.10(a) minimum) was captured. |
| Countercyclical capital buffer amount | Not numerically reproduced. |
| GSIB surcharge amounts / score bands | Not reproduced; only the existence of a subpart H calculation. |
| Community bank leverage ratio percentage (217.12) | Not reproduced. |
| Full "as amended" citation chain for §217.10 | Source-note tail not captured. |

## 8. Reviewer checklist

1. Confirm the "cited page" the requester had in mind; if it is a specific Federal Register amendment rather than the eCFR current page, re-verify §217.10(a)(1) against that document (all vintages checked here agree).
2. Confirm the institution's category (standardized vs. advanced approaches; Category I–IV) to decide whether the 3.0% SLR in 217.10(a)(1)(v) applies, and whether the binding risk-based ratio is the lower of standardized/advanced under 217.10(d).
3. Confirm the institution is not a qualifying community banking organization electing the 217.12 framework, which would supersede the four ratios above.
4. Confirm that the intended question excludes buffers; if the requester wanted the buffer-inclusive requirement, that is a different calculation under 217.11 (and, for GSIBs, subpart H) and is out of scope here.
5. Re-fetch and re-hash the sources at the date of use; the hashes above are point-in-time identifiers for the 2026-11-23T04:04Z fetch only.

## 9. Summary line

Under the text of 12 CFR 217.10(a)(1) as reproduced on the cited pages (eCFR current and govinfo CFR-2025/CFR-2026 annual editions, fetched 2026-11-23), and before any capital conservation buffer, countercyclical buffer, GSIB surcharge, leverage buffer or supervisory add-on, a Board-regulated institution must maintain a **common equity tier 1 capital ratio of 4.5 percent, a tier 1 capital ratio of 6 percent, a total capital ratio of 8 percent, and a leverage ratio of 4 percent** (plus, only if it is an advanced approaches or Category III institution, a supplementary leverage ratio of 3 percent).

*Draft prepared for professional review. Figures are quoted regulatory thresholds, not computed or audited amounts; the single computed figure (2.5% in Section 3) is an explicitly labelled illustration built on an assumed input.*

answer:
COMPLIANCE NOTE - EXTRACT FROM 17 CFR § 240.0-2(c) (Business hours of the Commission)
Prepared by: Compliance Specialist, Finance Office. Status: draft for review by a qualified finance/accounting professional; this is a verbatim-text extraction and control note, not legal, tax or investment advice. No repository, system or filing platform was accessed; the deliverable is this written extract.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
1. SOURCE RESOLUTION ('the cited page')
--------------------------------------------------------------------
The request does not name the page reproducing § 240.0-2(c). I therefore relied on the reproductions actually retrieved by the harness and verified they agree word-for-word:

  S1  eCFR, 17 CFR § 240.0-2 (current) - https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/part-240/section-240.0-2 ; fetched 2026-11-23T04:07:56Z ; sha256 f86928af7bf9
  S2  eCFR subject-group path (same section) - http://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-17/chapter-II/part-240/subpart-A/subject-group-ECFRf2ef38fa463cdfa/section-240.0-2 ; fetched 2026-11-23T04:07:56Z ; sha256 f86928af7bf9 (identical hash to S1)
  S3  GovInfo, CFR 2025 title 17 vol. 4, § 240.0-2, edition 2025-04-01 - https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title17-vol4/xhtml/CFR-2025-title17-vol4-sec240-0-2.html ; fetched 2026-11-23T04:07:55Z ; sha256 038795da7cb0 (XML variant sha256 7fa19039094a)
  S4  Federal Register, 88 FR 12209 (Feb. 27, 2023), doc. 2023-03931, amendatory instruction 10 revising § 240.0-2(c) - https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/full_text/html/2023/02/27/2023-03931.html ; fetched 2026-11-23T04:07:56Z ; sha256 f2abe034cd7a

Verification performed: S1, S2 and S3 reproduce paragraph (c) identically (character-for-character apart from the editorial heading 'Electronic filings.'), and S4 prints the same operative sentence as the text adopted by the 2023 amendment. Result: the answer below is invariant to which of these pages is treated as 'the cited page.' Source-statement history line appearing in all reproductions: [58 FR 14682, Mar. 18, 1993, as amended at 65 FR 24801, Apr. 27, 2000; 68 FR 25799, May 13, 2003; 73 FR 973, Jan. 4, 2008; 88 FR 12209, Feb. 27, 2023].

Period of the text relied on: current text as retrieved 2026-11-23 (eCFR current; GovInfo annual edition dated 2025-04-01). Currency: not applicable - no monetary amounts are involved. Basis: verbatim regulatory text; no interpretation beyond the plain words.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
2. VERBATIM TEXT OF § 240.0-2(c) (as reproduced on S1/S2/S3)
--------------------------------------------------------------------
"(c) Electronic filings. Filings made by direct transmission may be submitted to the Commission each day, except Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays, from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect."

Adjacent paragraphs, quoted only for contrast (they are different windows and are NOT the answer):
  (a) principal office open 9 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., except Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays;
  (b) paper submissions 8 a.m. to 5:30 p.m., except Saturdays, Sundays and federal holidays.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
3. ASK 2 - DAILY SUBMISSION WINDOW
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Window: 6:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m., Eastern Standard Time or Eastern Daylight Saving Time, whichever is currently in effect in Washington, DC.
Source: § 240.0-2(c), quoted verbatim in section 2 above (S1/S2/S3; confirmed by S4).
Arithmetic / basis of the figures: the two endpoints are clock times, not amounts. Window length = 22:00 − 06:00 = 16 hours. Check: 16 ≤ 24 (fits within one calendar day); 06:00 < 22:00 (endpoints ordered, no inversion).
Time-zone handling stated by the text itself: the window follows the Eastern Time offset actually in effect in Washington, DC, i.e. it shifts automatically between EST and EDT; no separate DST adjustment is required of the filer.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
4. ASK 4 - EXCLUDED DAYS
--------------------------------------------------------------------
Excluded (filings by direct transmission may not be submitted): Saturdays, Sundays, and Federal holidays.
Source: § 240.0-2(c), quoted verbatim in section 2 above.
Arithmetic / basis: 7 days per week − 2 weekend days = 5 eligible weekdays (Monday-Friday), further reduced by any Federal holiday falling on a weekday. Check: 5 ≤ 7.

Open item flagged for the reviewer (not resolved inside the cited text): § 240.0-2(c) says "Federal holidays" but does not enumerate them. The enumeration sits outside this paragraph (the federal-holiday list at 5 U.S.C. 6103 and the EDGAR Filer Manual's business-hours provisions are the usual references, together with the observed-holiday convention when a holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday). I have deliberately not imported a holiday calendar into the answer, because the ask is limited to the text of § 240.0-2(c); if the deliverable needs a dated holiday calendar for a specific filing year, that is a separate schedule and should be built and signed off separately.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
5. AMENDMENT CONTROL - DO NOT USE SUPERSEDED TEXT
--------------------------------------------------------------------
S4 (88 FR 12209, adopted Feb. 21, 2023, published Feb. 27, 2023) states: Rules 110(c), 0-2(c) and 0-5(c) previously provided '8 a.m. to 10 p.m.' and were revised to replace '8 a.m.' with '6 a.m.' to conform to 17 CFR 232.12(c) (Regulation S-T) and Section 2.3.1 of the EDGAR Filer Manual.
Control implication: any procedure, checklist or system configuration still stating an 8:00 a.m. opening for direct-transmission filings is out of date. Superseded window = 8 a.m. to 10 p.m. (14 hours: 22:00 − 08:00 = 14). Current window = 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. (16 hours). The 2-hour difference (16 − 14 = 2) is exactly the extension created by the amendment.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
6. COMPLIANCE POINTS A REVIEWER SHOULD CARRY FORWARD
--------------------------------------------------------------------
(i) Two different cutoffs, often conflated: the acceptance window (6 a.m.-10 p.m. ET) is not the same-business-day deemed-filing cutoff. S4 describes the Form 144 change as extending 'from 5:30 p.m. to 10:00 p.m. the latest time by which a filer can submit a direct transmission of a Form 144 to have it be deemed filed the same business day,' and quotes the general rule pair: submitted '[n]o later than 5:30 p.m., will be deemed filed on the same business day' and '[a]fter 5:30 p.m., will be deemed filed the next business day.' A filing accepted at, say, 8:00 p.m. is therefore accepted but generally deemed filed the next business day (subject to the specific form rule). Do not book an 8:00 p.m. acceptance as a same-day filing date.
(ii) Parallel provisions: 17 CFR 230.110(c) (Securities Act), 240.0-2(c) (Exchange Act) and 260.0-5(c) (Trust Indenture Act) all now read 6 a.m. to 10 p.m.; 17 CFR 232.12(c) (Regulation S-T) reads the same. Consistency check across all four is a cheap control.
(iii) The rule states when filings 'may be submitted'; it does not warrant that the Commission's systems will be available for the whole window. System availability is an operational matter (EDGAR Filer Manual / EDGAR status), not a representation in § 240.0-2(c).
(iv) Paragraphs (a) and (b) contain different hours (9:00 a.m.-5:30 p.m. for the principal office; 8:00 a.m.-5:30 p.m. for paper). Paper and electronic cutoffs must not be mixed in a single deadline table.

--------------------------------------------------------------------
7. LIMITATIONS
--------------------------------------------------------------------
This note reports regulatory text as reproduced on the pages cited in section 1, retrieved 2026-11-23. It is not legal advice and does not interpret the rule beyond its plain words. It does not include a dated federal-holiday calendar (see section 4 open item). Any downstream deadline engine, filing calendar or SOX-style control description built from this note should be reviewed by a qualified finance/accounting professional and, for legal reliance, by counsel.

question: Y143
answer:
COMPLIANCE NOTE — TRANSACTION REPORTING DEADLINE UNDER ARTICLE 26(1), REGULATION (EU) NO 600/2014 (ORIGINAL ADOPTED TEXT)
Prepared by: Compliance Officer, Finance Office. Status: draft for review by a qualified finance/legal professional. This note is a citation-and-deadline analysis of a regulatory reporting obligation. It is not financial, tax or investment advice, and it is not a legal opinion; the citation should be confirmed against the Official Journal PDF by the firm's Legal function before it is relied on in a control document.

=====================================================================
1. THE ANSWER (ASK 2)
=====================================================================
In the original text of Regulation (EU) No 600/2014, an investment firm that executes a transaction in a financial instrument must report complete and accurate details of that transaction to the competent authority AS QUICKLY AS POSSIBLE and, at the outer limit, NO LATER THAN THE CLOSE OF THE FOLLOWING WORKING DAY.

In plain terms: the deadline is T+1 working day — the close of the first working day after the day of execution.

=====================================================================
2. VERBATIM SOURCE TEXT (ASK 1 — ORIGINAL TEXT CONSTRAINT)
=====================================================================
Instrument: Regulation (EU) No 600/2014 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 15 May 2014 on markets in financial instruments and amending Regulation (EU) No 648/2012 (Text with EEA relevance).
Official Journal: OJ L 173, 12.6.2014, p. 84 et seq. (the exact OJ page of Article 26 to be confirmed from the PDF pagination; the PDF's own running heads in the captured pages read 'L 173/108', 'L 173/142', 'L 173/143').
Version used: 'Original (As adopted by EU)' — no amendments applied, per the page's own version banner.

Article 26(1), first subparagraph — quoted exactly:

  "Investment firms which execute transactions in financial instruments shall report complete and accurate details of such transactions to the competent authority as quickly as possible, and no later than the close of the following working day."

Article 26(1), second subparagraph (context, same source) — quoted exactly:

  "The competent authorities shall, in accordance with Article 85 of Directive 2014/65/EU, establish the necessary arrangements in order to ensure that the competent authority of the most relevant market in terms of liquidity for those financial instruments also receives that information."

Source trail for the two quotations above (four independent captures of the same sentence, all matching word-for-word):
  (a) https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2014/600/article/26/adopted — 'Original (As adopted by EU)' page, fetched 2026-11-23T04:10:21Z, sha256 3afbbd1054e3.
  (b) https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2014/600/pdfs/eur_20140600_adopted_en.pdf — the as-adopted OJ PDF, fetched 2026-11-23T04:10:22Z, sha256 24fae9245add.
  (c) https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2014/600/article/26 — UK-revised page, fetched 2026-11-23T04:10:21Z, sha256 4f46d9f0944b (first sentence identical).
  (d) https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eur/2014/600/article/26/2024-04-05/data.htm — point-in-time 05/04/2024, fetched 2026-11-23T04:10:22Z, sha256 1fe0c49afbad (first sentence identical).
Cross-check result: 4 of 4 captures agree on the operative sentence. No divergence in the deadline wording.

=====================================================================
3. HOW THE DEADLINE COMPUTES (ARITHMETIC SHOWN)
=====================================================================
Rule derived from the quoted words: deadline = close of business on the first working day strictly after the execution day.
Formula: Deadline = Execution date + 1 working day (counted in working days, not calendar days).
Worked examples (dates illustrative; only the weekday arithmetic is asserted, not any national holiday calendar):

  Execution day            +1 working day            Deadline (close of)
  Mon 2025-06-02           Tue 2025-06-03            Tue 2025-06-03
  Thu 2025-06-05           Fri 2025-06-06            Fri 2025-06-06
  Fri 2025-06-06           Mon 2025-06-09            Mon 2025-06-09 (weekend skipped)
  Sat 2025-06-07 (if any)  Mon 2025-06-09            Mon 2025-06-09

Check against the bound: every row is exactly one working day after execution — none is same-day (which would be stricter than the text) and none is two working days (which would breach the text).

Not stated by the text, and therefore not asserted here: any number of hours (e.g. 'T+24h'), any fixed clock time, any T+2 reading, and any definition of 'working day'. The quoted subparagraph does not define 'working day'; the applicable business calendar (weekends plus the relevant national/competent-authority public holidays) is a separate question to be confirmed against the Regulation's definitions and the relevant competent authority's guidance.

=====================================================================
4. SCOPE SO THE DEADLINE IS NOT QUOTED OUT OF CONTEXT
=====================================================================
- Who: 'Investment firms which execute transactions in financial instruments'. The obligation attaches to execution by an investment firm; it is not limited to on-venue execution (see paragraph 2 as described below).
- What: 'complete and accurate details' — completeness and accuracy are express, independent requirements alongside timeliness. A report filed on time but incomplete or inaccurate does not satisfy Article 26(1).
- Where it goes: 'to the competent authority'. Article 26(7), first sentence (quoted from the as-adopted page): "The reports shall be made to the competent authority either by the investment firm itself, an ARM acting on its behalf or by the trading venue through whose system the transaction was completed, in accordance with paragraphs 1, 3 and 9." Using an ARM or venue reporting does not extend the deadline.
- Correction of errors: Article 26(7) (as captured) provides that where there are errors or omissions in the transaction reports, the ARM, investment firm or trading venue reporting the transaction 'shall correct the information and submit a corrected report to the competent authority'. The original text as captured does not attach a separate numeric deadline to the correction; treat prompt correction as a control expectation and confirm with Legal.
- Instrument scope: Article 26(2) extends paragraph 1 to instruments admitted to trading or traded on a trading venue (or subject to a request for admission), instruments whose underlying is such an instrument, and instruments whose underlying is an index or basket of such instruments, and applies irrespective of whether the transaction is carried out on a trading venue. CAVEAT: the only captured text of paragraph 2 is the UK-revised version, which substitutes 'UK, Gibraltar or EU trading venue' for the original wording. The paragraph-2 wording above is therefore a description of structure, NOT a quotation of the 2014 text. Do not quote paragraph 2 as original without checking the OJ PDF.

=====================================================================
5. VERSION CONTROL — ORIGINAL 2014 TEXT vs LATER TEXTS
=====================================================================
- The ask is expressly limited to the original text adopted 15 May 2014, and the answer above is taken from that version (sources 2(a) and 2(b)).
- Observation only, not part of the answer: the same first sentence of Article 26(1) is unchanged in the UK-revised captures (2(c), 2(d)).
- Not verified here: the EU consolidated text at CELEX 02014R0600-20240109 (https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:02014R0600-20240109&qid=1709908589593) was listed as a source but returned no passage to this desk. If the firm needs the answer under the CURRENTLY APPLICABLE EU text rather than the 2014 original, that consolidated text must be read directly — it is outside the scope of this note and outside the ask.
- Jurisdiction: this note addresses the EU Regulation as adopted. Post-Brexit UK implementation, and any national competent authority operational cut-offs, are separate regimes and are not addressed.

=====================================================================
6. VERIFICATION POINTS FOR THE REVIEWER
=====================================================================

Tax year/period: 2025. Currency: USD. Basis: U.S. federal individual income tax, net investment income tax (NIIT) under IRC §1411 as described in IRS Publication 550 (2025). Status: draft for review by a qualified tax professional; not tax, legal or investment advice.

Source: IRS Publication 550 (2025), Investment Income and Expenses, 'For use in preparing 2025 Returns,' Investment Income chapter, General Information, 'Net investment income tax (NIIT).' URL: https://www.irs.gov/publications/p550; PDF: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p550.pdf. The publication states: 'The NIIT is a 3.8% tax on the lesser of your net investment income or the amount of your modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) that is over a threshold amount based on your filing status.' It then refers the reader to Code section 1411, Form 8960 and the Instructions for Form 8960.

1. Rate. The NIIT rate is 3.8%. Arithmetic: 3.8% = 3.8 / 100 = 0.038.

2. Amount to which the rate is applied. The 3.8% rate is applied to the lesser of:
   (a) net investment income (NII), as defined for §1411 / Form 8960; and
   (b) the excess, if any, of MAGI over the applicable filing-status threshold.

Formula: NIIT = 0.038 × min(NII, max(0, MAGI − T)), where T is the threshold amount for the taxpayer's filing status.

Threshold table from the same Pub. 550 (2025) passage:
- Married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse: T = $250,000.
- Married filing separately: T = $125,000.
- Single or head of household: T = $200,000.

These are the threshold amounts printed in the Pub. 550 (2025) NIIT passage. They are not taxpayer-specific amounts and no arithmetic is required to read them from the table.

3. Interpretation and arithmetic check. If MAGI is equal to or below T, the excess is zero and the NIIT is zero regardless of NII. If MAGI exceeds T, the rate applies only to the lesser of NII and the excess; it is not applied to all NII and it is not applied to MAGI itself.

Hypothetical arithmetic check, not a taxpayer return: assume a single filer with MAGI of $210,000 and NII of $8,000. Threshold T = $200,000. Excess = $210,000 − $200,000 = $10,000. Base = min($8,000, $10,000) = $8,000. NIIT = 0.038 × $8,000 = $304. The $8,000 base does not exceed either NII ($8,000) or the excess ($10,000), and the $304 result is 3.8% of the base.

Scope notes: The Pub. 550 passage is framed for individuals by filing status. Estates and trusts are subject to §1411 under separate threshold rules and are not covered by this individual-filer answer. For the NIIT base, use the §1411 / Form 8960 definition of net investment income; do not confuse it with the 'net investment income' computation used in Pub. 550 for the investment interest expense deduction. A dollar amount subject to NIIT cannot be determined without the taxpayer's filing status, NII and MAGI; the answer above gives the statutory rate and the statutory base to which it applies.

Prepared as a reference/checking aid for a qualified financial or accounting professional. Not regulatory, solvency, tax or investment advice. Every figure below carries its period, currency and basis.

=====================================================================
1. BOTTOM-LINE ANSWER
=====================================================================
- Probability: a confidence level of 99.5% (the Directive writes '99,5 %').
- Time horizon: one year ('over a one-year period').
- Equivalent ruin frequency: 0.5% per annum — i.e. a 1-in-200-year ruin event.
- Currency: none. All three numbers are dimentionless probabilities; there is no monetary amount in the calibration sentence.
- Basis: Value-at-Risk of the basic own funds of the undertaking.
- Caveat (read before citing): the Directive's text states the 99.5% confidence level. It does not, in the passages retrieved, use the phrase 'ruin frequency'. The 0.5% is the exact arithmetical complement of the stated confidence level, which is what 'equivalent ruin frequency' means. Cite Article 101(3) for the 99.5%/one-year wording and present 0.5% as a derivation, not as a quote.

=====================================================================
2. SOURCE AND VERSION CONTROL (satisfies ask 1)
=====================================================================
Text consulted: Directive 2009/138/EC of the European Parliament and of the Council of 25 November 2009 on the taking-up and pursuit of the business of Insurance and Reinsurance (Solvency II) (recast), English language version, in the 'Original (As adopted by EU)' version — the page states: 'The original version of the legislation as it stood when it was first adopted in the EU. No changes have been applied to the text.'
- Primary retrieval: https://www.legislation.gov.uk/eudr/2009/138/article/101/adopted (fetched 2026-11-23T04:16:51Z, sha256 ba9710f9c0bb).

I have not verified the text as it stands after the most recent Solvency II review; a reviewer should confirm against the current consolidated version before using this in a live regulatory filling.

=====================================================================
3. THE VERBATIM TEXT
=====================================================================
3.1 Article 101 ('Calculation of the Solvency Capital Requirement'), paragraph 3, second subparagraph — original adopted text:
   'It shall correspond to the Value-at-Risk of the basic own funds of an insurance or reinsurance undertaking subject to a confidence level of 99,5 % over a one-year period.'
   Source: legislation.gov.uk, Article 101, 'Original (As adopted by EU)' (sha256 ba9710f9c0bb). Note the EU formatting: decimal comma ('99,5') and a space before the percent sign.

3.2 Same Article, paragraph 3, first subparagraph (context — shows that the 12-month figure is a business-volume horizon, not the VaR horizon):
   'The Solvency Capital Requirement shall be calibrated so as to ensure that all quantifiable risks to which an insurance or reinsurance undertaking is exposed are taken into account. It shall cover existing business, as well as the new business expected to be written over the following 12 months. With respect to existing business, it shall cover only unexpected losses.'

3.3 Article 104(4) ('Design of the Basic Solvency Capital Requirement') — same calibration at module level:
   'Each of the risk modules referred to in paragraph 1 shall be calibrated using a Value-at-Risk measure, with a 99,5 % confidence level, over a one-year period.'
   Source: consolidated 2020-12-31 snippet (sha256 44b4df6bb8a1).

3.4 Article 122(1) ('Calibration standards') — confirms Article 101(3) is the reference calibration for internal models:
   '... may use a different time period or risk measure than that set out in Article 101(3) for internal modelling purposes as long as the outputs ... provide policy holders and beneficiaries with a level of protection equivalent to that set out in Article 101.'
   Source: consolidated 2013-12-19 page (sha256 ae36084bc4a6).

3.5 Not retrieved, therefore not cited: recital 62 (the recital normally paired with Article 101(3)) and Article 129 (Minimum Capital Requirement calibration). See section 6.

   Source: Article 101(3), quote 3.1 above.
   Period: one year. Currency: none (probability). Basis: VaR of basic own funds.

Step 2. Stated time horizon t = 1 year.
   Source: same sentence ('over a one-year period'). Period: one year. Currency: none. Basis: VaR horizon.

Step 4. Equivalent ruin frequency (return period) = 1 / p = 1 / 0.005 = 200 years.

SINGLE-COUNTERPARTY CREDIT LIMIT WORKPAPER — 12 CFR PART 252, SUBPART H
Draft for review by a qualified finance/regulatory-reporting professional. Not financial, tax or investment advice.

====================================================================
0. SCOPE, PERIOD, CURRENCY, BASIS
====================================================================
- Rule set: 12 CFR Part 252, Subpart H (Single-Counterparty Credit Limits), §§ 252.70–252.76, as in force 2026-11-21 (Ask 1 constraint).
- Entity: a "covered company" per § 252.70(a)(2)(i) — i.e., a global systemically important BHC, a Category II BHC, or a Category III BHC. (Classification is an assumption; see A-3.)
- Period: a single as-of date — the quarter-end reporting date as of which tier 1 capital is measured. The request supplies no date; all figures are treated as of one and the same date (A-4).
- Currency: USD, all inputs and outputs, no FX translation (A-6).
- Basis: regulatory tier 1 capital of the covered company (denominator of the test) and regulatory aggregate net credit exposure (ANCE) to one counterparty (numerator). Both on the regulatory measurement basis of Subpart H, not GAAP balance-sheet amounts.

====================================================================
1. AUTHORITY APPLIED, AND VERSION CONTROL FOR "AS IN FORCE ON 2026-11-21"
====================================================================
1.1 § 252.72(a) — Credit exposure limits, general limit (quoted verbatim):
    "No covered company may have an aggregate net credit exposure to any counterparty that exceeds 25 percent of the tier 1 capital of the covered company."
    Source: eCFR § 252.72 (fetched 2026-11-23T04:23:39Z, sha256 cfa98394af04); identical text in CFR 2025 print, 12 CFR Ch. II (1-1-25 Edition), at § 252.72 (sha256 5ae645463357).

1.2 § 252.72(b) — conditional higher-tier limit (quoted verbatim), carried here only so it is not overlooked:
    "No major covered company may have aggregate net credit exposure to any major counterparty that exceeds 15 percent of the tier 1 capital of the major covered company."
    § 252.70(a)(2)(ii): "Major covered company means any covered company that is a global systemically important BHC."
    Relevance: conditional on (i) the covered company being a GSIB BHC and (ii) the counterparty being a "major counterparty". Neither fact is given. See § 7 caveat C-1 and the sensitivity in § 5.

1.3 § 252.76(a)(1) — the 5% assessment trigger (quoted verbatim):
    "If a covered company has an aggregate net credit exposure to any counterparty that exceeds 5 percent of its tier 1 capital, the covered company must assess its relationship with the counterparty under paragraph (b)(2) of this section to determine whether the counterparty is economically interdependent with one or more other counterparties of the covered company and under paragraph (c)(1) of this section to determine whether the counterparty is connected by a control relationship with one or more other counterparties."
    Source: eCFR § 252.76 (fetched 2026-11-23T04:23:39Z, sha256 ca40090fa22e); identical in CFR 2025 print.

1.4 § 252.76(a)(2) — consequence of a positive assessment (quoted verbatim, abridged):
    "...the covered company must aggregate its net credit exposure to the counterparties for all purposes under this subpart, including, but not limited to, § 252.72."

1.5 Definition of economic interdependence (§ 252.76(b), quoted verbatim):
    "...two counterparties are economically interdependent if the failure, default, insolvency, or material financial distress of one counterparty would cause the failure, default, insolvency, or material financial distress of the other counterparty, taking into account the factors in paragraph (b)(2) of this section."

1.6 § 252.76(b)(2) factors retrieved verbatim (partial — see caveat C-3):
    (ii) whether counterparty A has fully or partly guaranteed the credit exposure of counterparty B, or is liable by other means, in an amount that is 50 percent or more of the covered company's net credit exposure to counterparty A;
    (iii) whether 25 percent or more of one counterparty's production or output is sold to the other counterparty, which cannot easily be replaced by other customers;
    (iv) whether the expected source of funds to repay the loans of both counterparties is the same and neither counterparty has another independent source of income from which the loans may be serviced and fully repaid;
    (v) whether two or more counterparties rely on the same source for the majority of their funding and, in the event of the common provider's default, an alternative provider cannot be found.

1.7 § 252.76(c)/(d) control-relationship indicia retrieved verbatim (§ 252.76(d)(2)): counterparty A (i) "Controls the power to vote 25 percent or more of any class of voting securities of Counterparty B pursuant to a voting agreement"; (ii) "Has significant influence on the appointment or dismissal of counterparty B's administrative, management, or governing body, or the fact that a majority of members of such body have been appointed solely as a result of the exercise of counterparty A's voting rights"; or (iii) "Has the power to exercise a controlling influence over the management or policies of counterparty B." The Board may also make its own aggregation determination under § 252.76(d)(1)–(2) after notice and opportunity for hearing.

1.8 Version-control statement. Both retrievals — the eCFR point-in-time-agnostic "current" text pulled 2026-11-23 (two days after the as-of date) and the CFR 2025 print (1-1-25 edition) — contain byte-identical operative language for §§ 252.72(a), 252.72(b) and 252.76(a)(1). Two consequences: (a) no amendment to these provisions took effect between 1 January 2025 and the 2026-11-21 as-of date on the evidence retrieved; (b) the quoted text is the text in force on 2026-11-21. Limitation: a complete amendatory-history check of Part 252 (Federal Register slips through 2026-11-21) was not performed; see caveat C-2. Subpart H source note: "83 FR 38493, Aug. 6, 2018, unless otherwise noted."

====================================================================
2. INPUTS AND PROVENANCE
====================================================================
Line | Input | Value | Unit | Source / basis | Status
I-1  | Tier 1 capital of the covered company (T1) | 40,000,000,000 | USD | Stated in the request | GIVEN
I-2  | Aggregate net credit exposure to the single counterparty (ANCE) | 11,000,000,000 | USD | Stated in the request | GIVEN
I-3  | General limit percentage | 25% (0.25) | ratio | § 252.72(a), verbatim § 1.1 | RULE
I-4  | Assessment trigger percentage | 5% (0.05) | ratio | § 252.76(a)(1), verbatim § 1.3 | RULE
I-5  | Conditional major-counterparty limit | 15% (0.15) | ratio | § 252.72(b), verbatim § 1.2 | RULE, conditionally applicable
I-6  | As-of date | single quarter-end | date | Assumed, not stated in request | ASSUMPTION A-4

Nothing in I-1 or I-2 is re-derived here: both are taken at face value as the regulatory measures. Whether they are in fact the correct regulatory measures is the subject of assumptions A-1, A-2, A-3, A-5.

====================================================================
3. COMPUTATION A — THE 25% CAP IN DOLLARS (Ask 2)
====================================================================
Formula (from § 252.72(a)):  Cap(25%) = 0.25 x T1
Step A-1: 0.25 x 40,000,000,000 = 10,000,000,000
Step A-2: Cap(25%) = USD 10,000,000,000 (= USD 10.0 billion)
Cross-check: 10,000,000,000 / 40,000,000,000 = 0.25 exactly. OK.

ANSWER TO ASK 2: USD 10,000,000,000 (USD 10.0 billion), being 25% of USD 40.0 billion of tier 1 capital, per § 252.72(a) as in force 2026-11-21.

====================================================================
4. COMPUTATION B — THE EXCESS OVER THE CAP (Ask 3)
====================================================================
Formula: Excess = ANCE - Cap(25%)
Step B-1: 11,000,000,000 - 10,000,000,000 = 1,000,000,000
Step B-2: Excess = USD 1,000,000,000 (= USD 1.0 billion) — a breach of § 252.72(a).

Supporting ratios (all derived from I-1/I-2, all internally consistent):
Step B-3: ANCE / T1 = 11,000,000,000 / 40,000,000,000 = 0.2750 = 27.50%
Step B-4: Percentage-point breach = 27.50% - 25.00% = 2.50 pp of tier 1 capital
Step B-5: Check B-4 against B-1: 2.50% x 40,000,000,000 = 1,000,000,000 = B-1. Consistent.
Step B-6: ANCE / Cap = 11,000,000,000 / 10,000,000,000 = 110.0% of the cap; i.e., the exposure is 10.0% above the cap.

ANSWER TO ASK 3: The exposure exceeds the 25% cap by USD 1,000,000,000 (USD 1.0 billion); ANCE is 110.0% of the cap and 27.50% of tier 1 capital.

====================================================================
5. COMPUTATION C — THE 5% ECONOMIC-INTERDEPENDENCE / CONTROL-RELATIONSHIP ASSESSMENT (Ask 4)
====================================================================
5.1 The test in § 252.76(a)(1) is purely arithmetic and purely a threshold test on ANCE versus 5% of tier 1 capital. It is NOT a 5% exposure cap: Subpart H contains no 5% ceiling on exposure. The 5% figure triggers a mandatory assessment and, if the assessment is positive, mandatory aggregation under § 252.76(a)(2).

5.2 Arithmetic:
Step C-1: Trigger threshold = 0.05 x T1 = 0.05 x 40,000,000,000 = 2,000,000,000
Step C-2: Test: is ANCE > threshold? 11,000,000,000 > 2,000,000,000 -> TRUE
Step C-3: Headroom / overage = 11,000,000,000 - 2,000,000,000 = 9,000,000,000 (exposure exceeds the 5% trigger by USD 9.0 billion)
Step C-4: ANCE / T1 = 27.50% (Step B-3) versus 5.00% -> 22.50 pp above the trigger; 5.50x the trigger (11.0 / 2.0).

5.3 Verdict: TRIGGERED. MEMORANDUM — ITEM 402(c) PERQUISITE ANALYSIS: EXCLUSION, QUANTIFICATION THRESHOLD, AND ITEM-BY-ITEM TEST

Prepared by: Accountant (draft for a qualified finance/accounting or securities professional to review). This is not legal, tax or investment advice.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
0. SCOPE, PERIOD, CURRENCY, BASIS, AUTHORITY
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- Registrant: an unnamed reporting company subject to Regulation S-K Item 402(c) executive compensation disclosure (full-form Summary Compensation Table). If the registrant is a smaller reporting company using the scaled table, see the note in §7 — the thresholds are the same.
- Period: a single fiscal year — the last completed fiscal year covered by the relevant proxy/information statement (assumed; the rule itself limits identification and quantification to 'compensation for the last fiscal year').
- Currency: US dollars (USD), assumed. All three given figures ($120,000; $24,000; $26,000) are treated as USD for the same fiscal year.
- Basis of measurement: aggregate incremental cost to the registrant, which is the mandated valuation basis for perquisites and personal benefits.
- Authority: 17 CFR 229.402 (Item 402). Text relied on was retrieved from eCFR 'current' on 2026-11-23T04:27:33Z (sha256 975472248ee6) and cross-checked against the 2024 and 2021 annual CFR editions on govinfo (sha256 18657eacefe1; bf0c17cb7b0e). All three carry identical language for the $10,000 exclusion gate and the $25,000 / 10% quantification test. Because the retrieved 'current' text — which reflects amendments effective on or before 2026-11-23 — contains no amendment to those thresholds, the text in force on 2026-11-21 is taken to be as quoted below. Verify against the Federal Register/CFR at the filing date before issuance.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. FACTS AS GIVEN
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
| Ref | Item | Amount (USD) | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | Total perquisites and personal benefits, one NEO, one fiscal year | 120,000 | Given |
| F2 | Item A | 24,000 | Given; assumed to be a perquisite/personal benefit |
| F3 | Item B | 26,000 | Given; assumed to be a perquisite/personal benefit |
| F4 | Residual other perquisites (derived) | 70,000 | 120,000 − 24,000 − 26,000 = 70,000 |
Tie-out: 24,000 + 26,000 + 70,000 = 120,000 ✓ (agrees to F1).
Assumed (flag for confirmation): neither F2 nor F3 is a tax reimbursement, an above-market-earnings item, a defined-benefit plan benefit, or an item reportable in another Summary Compensation Table column; and neither is an ordinary-course business item excluded from the perquisite definition. Either change alters the footnote treatment — see §6.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2. THE RULE, QUOTED (17 CFR 229.402)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
2.1 Inclusion/exclusion gate — aggregate < $10,000
- 'Perquisites and other personal benefits, or property, unless the aggregate amount of such compensation is less than $10,000' — enumeration within paragraph (c)(2)(ix).
- 'Perquisites and other personal benefits or property may be excluded only if the aggregate amount of such compensation will be less than $10,000. Individual perquisites and personal benefits shall be identified and quantified as required by Instruction 4 to paragraph (c)(2)(ix) of this Item.'

2.2 Instruction 4 to paragraph (c)(2)(ix) — the three-tier structure
'Perquisites and personal benefits may be excluded as long as the total value of all perquisites and personal benefits for a named executive officer is less than $10,000. If the total value of all perquisites and personal benefits is $10,000 or more for any named executive officer, then each perquisite or personal benefit, regardless of its amount, must be identified by type. If perquisites and personal benefits are required to be reported for a named executive officer pursuant to this rule, then each perquisite or personal benefit that exceeds the greater of $25,000 or 10% of the total amount of perquisites and personal benefits for that officer must be quantified and disclosed in a footnote. The requirements for identification and quantification apply only to compensation for the last fiscal year. Perquisites and other personal benefits shall be valued on the basis of the aggregate incremental cost to the registrant. With respect to the perquisite or other personal benefit for which footnote quantification is required, the registrant shall describe in the footnote its methodology for computing the aggregate incremental cost.'

2.3 Non-perquisite items reported in column (i)
'Any item reported for a named executive officer pursuant to paragraph (c)(2)(ix) of this Item that is not a perquisite or personal benefit and whose value exceeds $10,000 must be identified and quantified in a footnote to column (i).'

2.4 Tax reimbursements
Reimbursements of taxes owed with respect to perquisites or other personal benefits must be included in column (i) and are subject to separate quantification and identification as tax reimbursements even if the associated perquisites are excluded (aggregate < $10,000) or are identified but not separately quantified.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
3. APPLICATION — STEP BY STEP WITH ARITHMETIC
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Step 1 — Can the $120,000 be excluded altogether?
Test: F1 < $10,000?
120,000 < 10,000 → FALSE (120,000 ≥ 10,000).
Result: The exclusion is NOT available. The entire $120,000 is reported in column (i) 'All Other Compensation' of the Summary Compensation Table; no perquisite or personal benefit may be omitted from that column total.

Step 2 — Identification by type (applies because Step 1 failed)
Because the aggregate is ≥ $10,000, EACH perquisite or personal benefit, 'regardless of its amount', must be identified by type in a footnote to column (i) — including Item A ($24,000), Item B ($26,000), and every constituent of the $70,000 residual. Identification by type is required even where individual quantification is not.

Step 3 — Compute the footnote quantification threshold
10% prong: 0.10 × 120,000 = 12,000.
Greater-of test: max(25,000; 12,000) = 25,000.
Applicable threshold for this NEO = $25,000.
(Cross-check on which prong binds: the 10% prong exceeds $25,000 only when total perquisites exceed 25,000 ÷ 0.10 = 250,000. At exactly 250,000 the two prongs are equal (0.10 × 250,000 = 25,000). Since 120,000 < 250,000, the flat $25,000 prong governs here.)

Step 4 — Item-by-item quantification test (each item tested separately, not in aggregate)
| Item | Amount (USD) | Comparison with threshold | Exceeds? | Required treatment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Item A | 24,000 | 24,000 − 25,000 = (1,000) | No | Identify by type in footnote to column (i); no individual quantification |
| Item B | 26,000 | 26,000 − 25,000 = 1,000 | Yes | Quantify in footnote to column (i) AND describe the methodology for computing aggregate incremental cost |
| Residual perquisites | 70,000 total | Each constituent tested individually against 25,000 | Data-dependent | Identify each by type; quantify any single constituent exceeding 25,000 |
Note on the residual: the $70,000 is an aggregate of items not separately specified. The rule tests each perquisite individually, so a constituent of, e.g., $30,000 would require quantification even though the $24,000 item does not. Confirm the composition of the $70,000 before concluding that Item B is the only quantified item.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4. ANSWERS
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
4.1 May the registrant exclude perquisites altogether? — NO. Perquisites and personal benefits may be excluded only if the aggregate for the NEO is less than $10,000. Here the aggregate is $120,000 (120,000 ≥ 10,000), so the full $120,000 is included in column (i) and every perquisite is identified by type. The rule permits exclusion only below $10,000 in aggregate; it never permits omitting perquisites from the column when the aggregate reaches $10,000.

4.2 Footnote quantification threshold — $25,000. Derived as the greater of $25,000 or 10% of the NEO's total perquisites and personal benefits: max(25,000; 0.10 × 120,000 = 12,000) = $25,000.

4.3 Which item must be quantified — the $26,000 item. $26,000 > $25,000 (exceeds by $1,000), so it must be quantified in a footnote with a description of the aggregate incremental cost methodology. The $24,000 item does not exceed $25,000 (short by $1,000) and is identified by type only, not quantified.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
5. ILLUSTRATIVE FOOTNOTE (MODEL LANGUAGE — TO BE COMPLETED WITH ACTUAL TYPES AND COSTS)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
'Footnote to column (i) — Perquisites and Personal Benefits.
The amount reported in column (i) includes perquisites and other personal benefits with an aggregate incremental cost to the registrant of $120,000 for the fiscal year ended [date], valued on the basis of aggregate incremental cost. These consist of the following types: [type 1], [type 2], [type 3] and [type 4]. Because the aggregate value of perquisites and personal benefits equals or exceeds $10,000, each perquisite and personal benefit is identified by type regardless of amount. The [describe $26,000 item] had an aggregate incremental cost of $26,000, which exceeds the greater of $25,000 or 10% of total perquisites and personal benefits ($12,000), and is quantified as follows: $26,000, computed as [methodology — e.g., incremental charter hours × hourly rate + incremental catering = $X + $Y = $26,000]. The remaining perquisites and personal benefits are identified by type but not separately quantified because none individually exceeds $25,000, the greater of $25,000 and 10% of total perquisites and personal benefits ($12,000).'

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
6. SENSITIVITIES / WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
- If total perquisites were below $10,000: exclusion from column (i) would be available, but tax reimbursements on excluded perquisites would still require separate quantification.
- If total perquisites exceeded $250,000: the 10% prong would exceed $25,000 and would govern (threshold = 0.10 × total).
- If Item A ($24,000) were a tax reimbursement rather than a perquisite: it would require separate identification and quantification as a tax reimbursement irrespective of the $25,000 test.
- If Item A ($24,000) were a non-perquisite item reported in column (i): the separate $10,000 test for non-perquisite column (i) items would require its identification and quantification (24,000 > 10,000).
- If either item were an ordinary-course business item or otherwise outside the perquisite definition: it would drop out of the $120,000 base, changing the 10% prong (though not the $25,000 floor at these magnitudes).

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
7. SMALLER REPORTING COMPANY NOTE
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
The scaled smaller-reporting-company paragraph of Item 402 (paragraph (n), per the cross-references in the retrieved text) contains the same operative thresholds — exclusion only if the aggregate is less than $10,000, identification by type at $10,000 or more, and quantification of each item exceeding the greater of $25,000 or 10% of the officer's total perquisites. The conclusions in §4 therefore do not change; only the table (scaled Summary Compensation Table) and column reference change.

--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
8. OPEN DATA ITEMS (not rule gaps)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1. Confirm the nature of the $24,000 and $26,000 items (perquisite vs. personal benefit vs. tax reimbursement vs. other column (i) item).
2. Confirm the composition of the $70,000 residual and test each constituent against $25,000.
3. Confirm fiscal year, currency and that all amounts are aggregate incremental cost.
4. Confirm filer status (full-form vs. smaller reporting company) and confirm no intervening amendment to Item 402 between the retrieved text and 2026-11-21.

Prepared as a draft work product for review by a qualified professional; not legal, tax or investment advice.

# Corporation Tax: non-ring fence profits, rules from 1 April 2023

Draft for review by a qualified finance/accounting professional. Not financial, tax or investment advice.

## 1. Scope, period, currency, basis

| Item | Stated position |
|---|---|
| Tax | UK Corporation Tax (CT) |
| Profit stream | Non-ring fence profits only. Ring fence (oil extraction / oil rights, UK or UK continental shelf) is out of scope and its rates (19% small ring fence / 30% main ring fence / fraction 11/400) are excluded |
| Period | Financial year 2023 = **1 April 2023 to 31 March 2024**, and subsequent financial years on the same basis |
| Currency | GBP (£) |
| Basis of the figures | Taxable total profits of a UK-resident company for a single 12-month accounting period coincident with the financial year, with **no associated companies** and no exempt distributions of a qualifying kind (so augmented profits = taxable total profits). Adjustments for associated companies and short accounting periods are set out in section 6 |
| Sources | HMRC guidance as fetched (see section 8) |

## 2. Verdict (ask 4)

**No. From 1 April 2023 there is no longer a single Corporation Tax rate for non-ring fence profits.**

HMRC's words: *"From 1 April 2023, there is no longer a single Corporation Tax rate for non-ring fence profits."* (Corporation Tax rates and allowances guidance, sha256 8121e4a75038).

Corroboration: the same page's "Previous rates" text on the CT rates guide states *"From 1 April 2015 to 31 March 2023, a single rate of Corporation Tax applied to all companies"* (sha256 f9065dbe6492) — i.e. the single rate ended on 31 March 2023.

## 3. The rates (asks 5 and 6)

Per the HMRC rates table (column "2023", sha256 8121e4a75038), reproduced for the 2023 financial year:

| Band (taxable total profits, GBP, 12-month period, no associates) | Rate | Ask |
|---|---|---|
| £50,000 or less | **Small profits rate 19%** | 5 |
| Over £250,000 | **Main rate 25%** | 6 |
| £50,000 to £250,000 | Main rate 25% charged, then **reduced by marginal relief** | 7 |

Supporting quotes:
- *"A small profits rate of 19% was also announced for companies with profits of £50,000 or less."* (sha256 8121e4a75038)
- *"If your company made a profit of £50,000 or less, you'll pay the 'small profits rate', which is 19%."* (sha256 f9065dbe6492)
- *"If your company made more than £250,000 profit, you'll pay the main rate of Corporation Tax."* — the same page states *"The Corporation Tax rate for company profits is 25%"* (sha256 f9065dbe6492)
- *"From 1 April 2023 the Corporation Tax rate changes to: 19% for taxable profits below £50,000 (small profit rate); 25% for taxable profits above £250,000 (main rate)"* (Marginal Relief guidance, sha256 cc6f1af71f34)

Table parameters for FY2023 (sha256 8121e4a75038): Marginal Relief lower limit **£50,000**; upper limit **£250,000**; **standard fraction 3/200**.

Note on "£50,000 or less" vs "below £50,000": HMRC uses both formulations. It makes no difference — see the boundary proof at 4.2.

## 4. Treatment of profits between £50,000 and £250,000 (ask 7)

### 4.1 The rule

Profits in the band are charged at the **main rate of 25%**, and the resulting tax is **reduced by marginal relief**. Marginal relief produces a **gradual increase in the effective rate** from 19% to 25%.

HMRC's words:
- *"Companies with profits between £50,000 and £250,000 will pay tax at the main rate, reduced by a marginal relief. This provides a gradual increase in the effective Corporation Tax rate."* (sha256 8121e4a75038)
- *"You may be entitled to 'Marginal Relief' if your profits were between £50,000 and £250,000."* (sha256 f9065dbe6492)
- *"Marginal Relief provides a gradual increase in Corporation Tax rate between the small profits rate and the main rate — this allows you to reduce your rate from the 25% main rate."* (sha256 cc6f1af71f34)
- CTM03905: *"Where profits fall between the lower and upper limits, the total taxable profits are charged at the main rate of CT and the resulting tax is reduced by a sum of marginal relief computed by applying a 'standard fraction' to an amount..."* (sha256 fb3fe1275f68)

### 4.2 Marginal relief computation

Statutory form (CTA 2010 Part 3A), applied with the FY2023 standard fraction **3/200 = 0.015 = 1.5%**:

> Marginal relief = (U − A) × N/A × 3/200

where U = upper limit (£250,000), A = augmented profits, N = taxable total profits. Where there are no exempt distributions of a qualifying kind, A = N and the formula simplifies to:

> **Marginal relief = (250,000 − P) × 3/200**, and **CT = 0.25 × P − (250,000 − P) × 0.015**

Equivalently, in closed form for 50,000 ≤ P ≤ 250,000: **CT = 0.265 × P − 3,750**.

Provenance note: the fetched passages state the fraction (3/200) and the direction of the relief, and CTM03958's worked example applies the fraction to (upper limit − profits) — i.e. the (U − A) × F form. The full statutory wording of CTA10 s18C was not in the fetched passages; the formula above should be confirmed against the statute by the reviewer.

**Boundary proofs (these are the consistency tests for asks 5, 6 and 7):**

- At P = £50,000: 25% × 50,000 = £12,500.00; relief = (250,000 − 50,000) × 0.015 = 200,000 × 0.015 = £3,000.00; CT = £9,500.00. Check: 19% × 50,000 = £9,500.00. **Agrees exactly with the ask-5 rate — no discontinuity at the lower limit.**
- At P = £250,000: relief = (250,000 − 250,000) × 0.015 = £0.00; CT = 25% × 250,000 = £62,500.00. **Agrees exactly with the ask-6 rate — no discontinuity at the upper limit.**
- Marginal rate in the band: d/dP of (0.25P − (250,000 − P)(0.015)) = 0.25 + 0.015 = **0.265 = 26.5%**. Checked by step: P = 100,000 → CT £22,750.00; P = 100,100 → 25,025.00 − (149,900 × 0.015 = 2,248.50) = £22,776.50; Δ = £26.50 on £100 = 26.5%. ✔
- Below the lower limit the relief formula is **not** applied. At P = £40,000: 19% × 40,000 = £7,600.00. (The relief formula would give 10,000 − 210,000 × 0.015 = £6,850, which is lower — so the small profits rate, not relief, governs below £50,000.)

### 4.3 Schedule of CT — FY2023, non-ring fence, 12-month period, no associated companies

All figures GBP. Arithmetic shown in full.

| P = taxable total profits | 25% × P (main rate) | Marginal relief (250,000 − P) × 0.015 | CT due | Effective rate (CT / P) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 40,000 (below band) | n/a — 19% applies | n/a | **7,600.00** (19% × 40,000) | 19.000% |
| 50,000 (lower limit) | 12,500.00 | 200,000 × 0.015 = 3,000.00 | **9,500.00** | 19.000% |
| 60,000 | 15,000.00 | 190,000 × 0.015 = 2,850.00 | **12,150.00** | 20.250% |
| 75,000 | 18,750.00 | 175,000 × 0.015 = 2,625.00 | **16,125.00** | 21.500% |
| 100,000 | 25,000.00 | 150,000 × 0.015 = 2,250.00 | **22,750.00** | 22.750% |
| 150,000 | 37,500.00 | 100,000 × 0.015 = 1,500.00 | **36,000.00** | 24.000% |
| 200,000 | 50,000.00 | 50,000 × 0.015 = 750.00 | **49,250.00** | 24.625% |
| 250,000 (upper limit) | 62,500.00 | 0 × 0.015 = 0.00 | **62,500.00** | 25.000% |
| 300,000 (above band) | 75,000.00 | none | **75,000.00** | 25.000% |

Cross-checks: closed form 0.265P − 3,750 gives 9,500 / 22,750 / 62,500 at P = 50,000 / 100,000 / 250,000 — ties to the table. Every effective rate lies within [19%, 25%]; CT is monotonically increasing in P across all rows (7,600 → 9,500 → 12,150 → 16,125 → 22,750 → 36,000 → 49,250 → 62,500 → 75,000). Effective rate = 26.5% − 3,750/P inside the band.

### 4.4 Who cannot claim marginal relief

Per the Marginal Relief guidance (sha256 cc6f1af71f34): not available to a **non-UK resident company**, a **close investment-holding company**, or where profits (including distributions from unrelated, unassociated companies) exceed **£250,000**. CTM03905 (sha256 fb3fe1275f68) confirms the small profits rate/marginal relief scope excludes close investment-holding companies (CTA10/S18N).

## 5. Accounting periods straddling 1 April 2023

Where more than one rate applies in an accounting period, split the period by days and compute each part separately (sha256 f9065dbe6492). HMRC's own example: an accounting period 1 January 2023 to 31 December 2023 uses the financial year starting 1 April 2022 rate for **90 days** (1 Jan–31 Mar 2023) and the financial year starting 1 April 2023 rate for **275 days** (1 Apr–31 Dec 2023). 90 + 275 = 365. ✔

## 6. Threshold adjustments (limits on the figures above)

HMRC: *"The £50,000 and £250,000 profit thresholds are proportionately reduced for short accounting periods and by the total number of 'associated companies' your company has"* (sha256 f9065dbe6492).

- **Short accounting period:** apportion the £50,000 / £250,000 limits by reference to the number of days in the period over 365. Example: 6-month (182-day) period → lower limit 50,000 × 182/365 = £24,931.51; upper limit 250,000 × 182/365 = £124,657.53.
- **Associated companies:** the limits are reduced by reference to the number of associated companies. *Illustrative, and to be confirmed against CTA10 s18D by the reviewer* (the fetched gov.uk text says only "by the total number of associated companies"): on the (1 + number of associates) convention, one associate gives lower £25,000 / upper £125,000; two associates give £16,666.67 / £83,333.33; and one associate with a 182-day period gives £12,465.75 / £62,328.77.
- **Augmented profits:** the upper-limit test uses augmented profits (taxable total profits plus exempt distributions of a qualifying kind that are not excluded — CTA10/S18L, per CTM03905, sha256 fb3fe1275f68). The relief formula's A term is augmented profits; N is taxable total profits.

All of section 4's figures assume no associated companies and a 12-month period, as stated in section 1.

## 7. Version control and two traps in the source pages

1. **Stale line:** the "Show all updates" list on the rates-and-allowances publication page (sha256 d589956a9326) contains a 3 October 2022 entry reading *"The Corporation Tax main rate will remain at 19% from 1 April 2023."* That was **superseded** by the 21 December 2022 entry on the same page: *"From 1 April 2023 there is no longer a single Corporation Tax rate for non-ring fence profits. Marginal relief is also available for companies with profits between £50,000 and £250,000."* The current table (19% / 25% / £50,000 / £250,000 / 3/200) governs. Do not use the 3 October 2022 line.
2. **Illustrative future example, not FY2023:** CTM03958 (sha256 7c01dd11e1de) works an example for a period 1 July 2030 to 30 June 2031 with an upper limit of **£300,000** and fraction **3/250**. That is a hypothetical future-year illustration. For FY2023 the upper limit is £250,000 and the fraction is 3/200. Do not import 3/250 or £300,000.
3. **Which version?** The guidance page is marked "Updated 1 April 2026". The 2023, 2024, 2025 and 2026 columns of the table all show the same values (small profits 19%, main 25%, lower limit £50,000, upper limit £250,000, standard fraction 3/200). The FY2023 answer is therefore unaffected by using the current version of the page.

## 8. Sources

All fetched 2026-11-23.

| Ref | Page | sha256 | Supports |
|---|---|---|---|
| [1] | https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/rates-and-allowances-corporation-tax/rates-and-allowances-corporation-tax | 8121e4a75038 | Rates table (19% / 25% / £50,000 / £250,000 / 3/200); "no longer a single Corporation Tax rate"; marginal relief description; ring fence rates excluded |
| [2] | https://www.gov.uk/corporation-tax-rates | f9065dbe6492 | 25% main rate; 19% small profits rate; marginal relief band; threshold reduction for short periods and associates; 90/275-day straddle example; single rate 1 Apr 2015–31 Mar 2023 |
| [3] | https://www.gov.uk/guidance/corporation-tax-marginal-relief | cc6f1af71f34 | 19% / 25%; relief mechanism; who cannot claim |
| [4] | https://www.gov.uk/hmrc-internal-manuals/company-taxation-manual/ctm03905 | fb3fe1275f68 | Statutory basis (CTA10 Part 3A, FA2021/S6 and SCH1); main-rate-plus-relief mechanism; standard fraction; augmented profits definition (CTA10/S18L); CIC exclusion (CTA10/S18N) |
| [5] | https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/rates-and-allowances-corporation-tax | d589956a9326 | Update history; 21 Dec 2022 change; the superseded 3 Oct 2022 line |
| [6] | https://www.gov.uk/hmrc-internal-manuals/company-taxation-manual/ctm03958 | 7c01dd11e1de | Confirms the fraction is applied to (upper limit − profits); source of the FY2031 £300,000 / 3/250 illustration that must not be used for FY2023 |

## 9. Answer in one line

From 1 April 2023 there is **no** single CT rate for non-ring fence profits: **19%** on profits of £50,000 or less, **25%** on profits above £250,000, and for profits between £50,000 and £250,000 tax is charged at the **25% main rate reduced by marginal relief** at the standard fraction **3/200** (marginal rate 26.5%; CT = 0.265P − 3,750 for a 12-month period with no associated companies).

*Draft prepared for professional review. Figures are GBP, FY2023 (1 April 2023 – 31 March 2024) basis, non-ring fence, 12-month accounting period, no associated companies. Thresholds must be re-scaled for short accounting periods and associated companies before any figure is applied to a real company.*
